federal-reserve.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

sections.title: Volatility & internals
sections.description: How much the index and its constituents may move, and whether those moves reinforce or cancel one another.

sections.title: Breadth & leadership
sections.description: Whether market performance is broadly shared or carried by a narrow set of companies and sectors.

sections.title: Credit & liquidity
sections.description: Whether financing stress is spreading beyond equities into credit conditions and market liquidity.

sections.title: Rates & inflation
sections.description: The discount-rate and inflation backdrop that transmits macro changes into asset valuations.

sections.title: Growth & cycle
sections.description: Slower-moving evidence on employment, growth and where the economy sits in the business cycle.

sections.title: Cross-asset confirmation
sections.description: Whether currencies and other markets confirm the regime seen in equities, rates and credit.

VIX.name: Cboe Volatility Index
VIX.description: Annualized expected 30-day volatility of the S&P 500 index.
VIX.howToRead: Higher values mean larger index moves are being priced. VIX describes expected movement size, not whether the market will rise or fall.

historyStatus.note: The modern-method pre-2003 history was reconstructed by Cboe.

VIXEQ.name: Cboe S&P 500 Constituent Volatility Index
VIXEQ.description: Annualized market-cap-weighted 30-day implied volatility of eligible S&P 500 constituents.
VIXEQ.howToRead: Higher values mean larger individual-stock moves are being priced, even when opposing moves keep the index comparatively calm.

DSPX.name: Cboe S&P 500 Dispersion Index
DSPX.description: Annualized expected 30-day idiosyncratic movement among S&P 500 constituents.
DSPX.howToRead: Higher values indicate greater expected differentiation between stocks and more scope for opposing moves to cancel at index level.

COR1M.name: Cboe 1-Month Implied Correlation Index
COR1M.description: Expected one-month co-movement among the largest S&P 500 constituents.
COR1M.howToRead: High values mean large stocks are expected to move together and diversification may weaken. Low values imply more independent moves.

VIX9D.name: Cboe S&P 500 9-Day Volatility Index
VIX9D.description: Annualized expected nine-day volatility of the S&P 500 index.
VIX9D.whyAdd: Starts the volatility curve and reveals front-loaded event stress that a 30-day reading can hide.

VIX1D.name: Cboe 1-Day Volatility Index
VIX1D.whyAdd: Separates immediate event risk from the standard 30-day VIX horizon.

VIX3M.name: Cboe S&P 500 Three-Month Volatility Index
VIX3M.description: Annualized expected three-month volatility of the S&P 500 index.
VIX3M.whyAdd: Creates a simple volatility term structure when compared with VIX and VIX9D.

VVIX.name: Cboe VVIX Index
VVIX.description: Option-implied uncertainty about the expected volatility of the VIX.
VVIX.whyAdd: Shows how uncertain the options market is about the VIX itself.

SKEW.name: Cboe SKEW Index
SKEW.whyAdd: Adds information about the relative pricing of large downside moves that VIX alone does not show.

OFRVOL.name: OFR Financial Stress Index: Volatility contribution
OFRVOL.description: Volatility-category contribution to the OFR Financial Stress Index.
OFRVOL.howToRead: Positive values add volatility-related stress to the aggregate OFR FSI; negative values offset it. This is a signed contribution, not an implied-volatility percentage.

BREADTH200.name: S&P 500 members above their 200-day average
BREADTH200.whyAdd: Tests whether an index move is supported by a broad majority of constituents.

RSP_SPY.name: Equal-weight versus cap-weight relative strength
RSP_SPY.whyAdd: Shows whether the average stock is keeping pace with the largest index constituents.

OFREQUITY.name: OFR Financial Stress Index: Equity valuation contribution
OFREQUITY.description: Equity-valuation contribution to the OFR Financial Stress Index.
OFREQUITY.howToRead: Positive values mean equity-valuation conditions are adding to financial stress; negative values mean they are offsetting it. This does not measure stock-market returns.

OFRFSI.name: OFR Financial Stress Index
OFRFSI.description: A daily market-based measure of stress across global financial markets, centered around zero.
OFRFSI.howToRead: The index is centered around zero. Positive values indicate above-average financial stress and negative values indicate below-average stress. Category contributions show where it originates.

OFRCREDIT.name: OFR Financial Stress Index: Credit contribution
OFRCREDIT.description: Credit-market contribution to the OFR Financial Stress Index.
OFRCREDIT.howToRead: Positive values mean credit conditions are adding to broad stress. A rise alongside funding stress is stronger evidence that pressure is spreading.
OFRCREDIT.whyAdd: Tests whether equity and options stress is spreading into credit markets.

OFRFUNDING.name: OFR Financial Stress Index: Funding contribution
OFRFUNDING.description: Funding-market contribution to the OFR Financial Stress Index.
OFRFUNDING.howToRead: Positive values mean funding and liquidity conditions are adding to stress. A rise alongside credit stress is stronger evidence of broad transmission.
OFRFUNDING.whyAdd: Distinguishes an equity-local shock from stress in funding and short-term liquidity channels.

HY_OAS.name: ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread
HY_OAS.whyAdd: Confirms whether equity stress is spreading into the cost of financing for lower-quality borrowers.

NFCI.name: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index
NFCI.whyAdd: Adds a broad weekly check on risk, credit and leverage conditions.

CURVE2S10S.name: 10-Year Treasury minus 2-Year Treasury spread
CURVE2S10S.description: Dashboard-calculated same-date difference between the 10-year and 2-year Treasury constant-maturity yields.
CURVE2S10S.whyAdd: Adds cycle context and distinguishes market stress from a change in the rates regime.
CURVE2S10S.observationSemantics: Dashboard calculation: 100 × (DGS10 minus DGS2) on dates where both inputs are available

DGS2.name: 2-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate
DGS2.description: Daily market yield on U.S. Treasury securities at two-year constant maturity.
DGS2.whyAdd: Provides the policy-sensitive short-rate input for the yield-curve slope.
DGS2.observationSemantics: Federal Reserve H.15 daily constant-maturity yield

DGS10.name: 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate
DGS10.description: Daily market yield on U.S. Treasury securities at ten-year constant maturity.
DGS10.whyAdd: Provides the long-rate input for curve and rate-volatility context.
DGS10.observationSemantics: Federal Reserve H.15 daily constant-maturity yield

RATEVOL20.name: 20-Observation Realized 10-Year Treasury Yield Volatility
RATEVOL20.description: Dashboard-calculated sample volatility of the latest 20 valid daily changes in DGS10.
RATEVOL20.whyAdd: Shows whether the rates backdrop is unusually unstable even when the yield level itself is not extreme.
RATEVOL20.observationSemantics: Dashboard calculation: sample standard deviation of the latest 20 DGS10 changes in basis points

calculation.formula: sample standard deviation of latest 20 changes in 100 × DGS10

REAL10Y.name: 10-Year Treasury real yield
REAL10Y.whyAdd: Shows the inflation-adjusted discount rate applied to long-duration assets.

T10YIE.name: 10-Year Breakeven Inflation Rate
T10YIE.whyAdd: Separates changes in nominal yields into real-rate and inflation-expectation components.

T5YIFR.name: 5-Year, 5-Year Forward Inflation Expectation Rate
T5YIFR.description: Market-implied average inflation over the five-year period beginning five years ahead.
T5YIFR.whyAdd: Helps separate an inflation or term-premium shock from a growth or liquidity shock.
T5YIFR.observationSemantics: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis calculated inflation-expectation rate

ICSA.name: Initial Claims
ICSA.whyAdd: Adds a timely weekly check on whether market stress is reaching the real economy.

WEI.name: Dallas Fed Weekly Economic Index
WEI.description: Weekly estimate of the common component of ten high-frequency U.S. activity series, scaled to four-quarter GDP growth.
WEI.whyAdd: Tests whether a market regime is reaching high-frequency real-economy activity.
WEI.observationSemantics: Dallas Fed model estimate scaled to four-quarter GDP growth

DTWEXBGS.name: Nominal Broad U.S. Dollar Index
DTWEXBGS.description: Trade-weighted foreign-exchange value of the U.S. dollar against a broad group of major trading partners.
DTWEXBGS.whyAdd: A stronger broad dollar can confirm that equity or funding stress is becoming a global tightening event.
DTWEXBGS.observationSemantics: Federal Reserve broad nominal dollar index

relationships.label: Constituent variance feeds dispersion
relationships.explanation: When expected single-stock variance rises relative to index variance, implied dispersion tends to rise.

relationships.label: Index variance offsets dispersion
relationships.explanation: All else equal, more index variance leaves less of the constituent variance difference classified as dispersion.

relationships.label: Independent moves versus co-movement
relationships.explanation: High dispersion with low implied correlation is consistent with large stock moves cancelling inside the index.

relationships.label: Co-movement can expose index volatility
relationships.explanation: If correlation rises while constituent volatility is already high, fewer stock moves cancel and index volatility can become more visible.

relationships.label: Near-term risk versus 30-day risk
relationships.explanation: Comparing VIX9D with VIX separates front-loaded event risk from the broader one-month outlook.

relationships.label: Short stress versus persistent stress
relationships.explanation: The VIX to VIX3M slope helps distinguish a brief shock from sustained volatility expectations.

relationships.label: Uncertainty about volatility
relationships.explanation: High VVIX can show fragile or rapidly changing volatility expectations even before VIX reaches an extreme.

relationships.label: Breadth qualifies dispersion
relationships.explanation: Weak breadth with high dispersion can indicate that a narrow group is carrying the index while many stocks lag.

relationships.label: Volatility contributes to broad stress
relationships.explanation: The published volatility category is one component of the aggregate OFR Financial Stress Index.

relationships.label: Equity valuation contributes to broad stress
relationships.explanation: The published equity-valuation category is one component of the aggregate OFR Financial Stress Index.

relationships.label: Credit contributes to broad stress
relationships.explanation: The published credit category is one component of the aggregate OFR Financial Stress Index.

relationships.label: Funding contributes to broad stress
relationships.explanation: The published funding category is one component of the aggregate OFR Financial Stress Index.

relationships.label: Credit confirms or rejects equity stress
relationships.explanation: A rising OFR credit contribution alongside high equity volatility suggests stress is spreading beyond options markets.

relationships.label: Funding stress can synchronize risk
relationships.explanation: Rising funding stress can turn a stock-specific regime into a broader shock in which correlations increase.

relationships.label: The dollar tests global tightening
relationships.explanation: A strengthening broad dollar can confirm that funding stress is becoming a global tightening event.

relationships.label: Growth distinguishes rotation from contraction
relationships.explanation: Stable weekly growth with calm credit supports an idiosyncratic rotation story, while weakening growth and rising credit stress point toward a macro regime.

relationships.label: The curve adds cycle context
relationships.explanation: The yield-curve slope is a slow cycle signal. Its message is more useful when compared with the direction of high-frequency economic activity.

relationships.label: Inflation pricing qualifies volatility
relationships.explanation: Rising long-run inflation pricing alongside equity volatility supports a rates or inflation shock more than a pure growth scare.

relationships.label: Real rates shape equity leadership
relationships.explanation: Changes in real yields can help explain whether narrow leadership reflects a shifting discount-rate regime.

regimes.title: High dispersion, contained systemic stress
regimes.copy: The local options layer shows elevated constituent volatility and dispersion with low implied correlation, while the public OFR aggregate, credit and funding readings are not historically elevated. This is more consistent with stock-specific rotation than broad financial-system stress.

regimes.title: Systemic stress is confirming the market signal
regimes.copy: The local options layer shows elevated index volatility and implied correlation, while the public OFR aggregate is also historically elevated. Market co-movement and broader financial stress are reinforcing the same risk story.

regimes.title: Calm surface, restless undercurrents
regimes.copy: Index volatility is not elevated, while stock-level volatility and dispersion are high and implied correlation is low. This is consistent with large, offsetting single-stock moves.

regimes.title: Synchronized risk is visible
regimes.copy: Index volatility and co-movement are both elevated relative to history, which is consistent with a broader, more systematic risk regime.

regimes.title: A broadly subdued volatility regime
regimes.copy: Index volatility, stock-level volatility and dispersion are all low relative to their compatible historical windows.

regimes.title: Broad financial stress is elevated
regimes.copy: The aggregate OFR Financial Stress Index is in the upper quarter of its compatible history. Its category contributions show which channels are adding to or offsetting the pressure.

regimes.title: Broad financial stress is subdued
regimes.copy: The aggregate OFR Financial Stress Index is in the lower quarter of its compatible history. Individual category contributions can still diverge, so the calm aggregate should not be read as an absence of all risk.

regimes.title: Financial-stress signals are mixed
regimes.copy: The aggregate OFR reading is not historically extreme. Its category contributions show where stress is accumulating and where pressures are offsetting one another.
